title: ManorManager
summary: A multi-tenant property operations platform for organisations managing buildings, maintenance, leasing, billing and subscriptions.
description: ManorManager is a multi-tenant property operations management platform designed to help property owners, estate operators and facilities teams coordinate buildings, units, assets, maintenance, contractors, leasing, invoicing and subscription entitlements.
problem: Property operations are often split across spreadsheets, email threads and disconnected tools, making it difficult to maintain accurate asset records, coordinate maintenance, track contractors and understand portfolio-wide financial and operational activity. Multi-organisation software also requires strict separation of each organisation's data.
solution: I am building ManorManager as an organisation-aware property operations platform with tenant-scoped access and shared workflows for property structures, units, assets, work orders, preventive maintenance, contractors, leasing, invoices, payments and subscriptions.
contributions: Designed and implemented the .NET solution and major business domains, including identity, organisations, properties, maintenance, leasing, billing and subscriptions. Established Clean Architecture boundaries, organisation-aware persistence and access rules, owner safeguards, PostgreSQL advisory-lock concurrency controls, provider integrations, CI workflows and architectural, unit and database integration tests.
architecture: ManorManager uses Clean Architecture within a modular monolith. The Domain layer owns entities and business rules, Application coordinates use cases, Infrastructure implements persistence and external providers, and the API is the HTTP composition root. The backend uses .NET 10, C# 13, ASP.NET Core, EF Core 10 and PostgreSQL. Paystack, Cloudinary, Cloudflare R2 and Zoho SMTP are isolated behind infrastructure interfaces.
challenges: The central challenge was preventing tenant data leakage across organisations. The implementation combines explicit organisation context, tenant-aware entities, global query filters, write validation and composite relationships. Advisory locks protect concurrent resource operations, while webhook verification and provider abstractions reduce risk around payments and external storage.
outcomes: Established a modular .NET 10 backend covering organisations, properties, assets, maintenance, contractors, leasing, billing and subscriptions. Delivered organisation-level isolation, concurrency safeguards, provider integrations, architecture tests, database integration tests and a documented, phase-based roadmap.

title: Pro Residance Applications
summary: A role-based student residence application and administration platform for managing applicants, preferences, reviews and allocations.
description: Suburban Digs Residence Applications is a full-stack platform for student accommodation applications and administration. Students discover residences, maintain profiles, submit ordered residence preferences and track applications. Managers and administrators manage properties, application periods, reviews and residence allocations.
problem: Residence applications involve time-sensitive cycles, supporting documents, preference ordering and decisions made by several roles. Manual processes can make application status and required actions unclear, while academic-year cycles should be configurable without software releases.
solution: I built a centralised Next.js application with student, residence manager, admissions administrator and system administrator experiences. MongoDB stores application records and dynamic periods, Cloudflare R2 protects private student documents, Cloudinary serves public residence imagery, and Better Auth provides role-aware access.
contributions: Designed and developed the App Router application, MongoDB models and Mongoose services. Implemented Better Auth roles, server-side ownership and authorisation checks, Zod validation, dynamic application periods, preference and application integrity rules, allocation workflows, signed private-document storage and application email communication.
architecture: The system uses a server-oriented Next.js architecture. App Router pages and role-specific portals call authenticated route handlers and server actions. Feature services apply Zod validation, role and ownership checks, and Mongoose persistence before touching MongoDB. Better Auth manages sessions, with private R2 documents and public Cloudinary residence media kept in separate storage boundaries.
challenges: Application periods had to support successive academic years, so they are stored as managed records rather than hard-coded dates. Database and server rules prevent duplicate applications, residence preferences and preference positions. Private student files use signed R2 operations, while public residence photography uses separate public delivery.
outcomes: Delivered student, manager, admissions and system-administrator workflows with dynamic application periods, validated preferences, application reviews, residence allocations and separated private/public storage. A production deployment is available at the Suburban Digs application domain.

title: Rezora
summary: A controlled digital voting platform with eligibility checks, campaign administration and database-enforced one-vote-per-category rules.
description: Rezora is a digital voting platform built for the Affinity Student Living Gala Awards. It provides verified ballot submission for eligible student residents and administrative tools for residences, campaigns, voting categories, nominees and voter enrolment.
problem: Residence awards voting needs accessible participation while preventing duplicate ballots and protecting election integrity. Live totals could also influence public voting behaviour, so campaign statistics must remain separate from public nominee data.
solution: I developed a role-based Next.js application for voters and administrators. Voting eligibility is checked by account verification and residence assignment, while a compound MongoDB unique index enforces one ballot per voter, campaign and category even under concurrent submissions.
contributions: Built the Next.js application, Better Auth roles, voter eligibility, campaign and nominee management, ballot submission, residence-category rules, Excel and CSV enrolment, administrator statistics, audit records, migration and integrity scripts, and Cloudinary/Nodemailer integrations.
architecture: Rezora uses a server-oriented Next.js architecture with App Router route handlers and dedicated campaign and voting services. Better Auth provides the actor context, Zod validates requests, and Mongoose persists campaign, residence, category, nominee, voter and ballot records in MongoDB. Public responses exclude live administrator-only statistics.
challenges: Repeated and concurrent ballot submissions required a database-level guarantee, not only frontend or service checks. A compound unique index on voter, campaign and category protects the rule. Campaign lifecycle states, residence eligibility and category assignment add further boundaries, while historical voter data required migration and deduplication tooling.
outcomes: Built a complete voting workflow with role-based access, residence-based category eligibility, campaign controls, database-enforced ballot uniqueness, restricted statistics, voter imports, audit records and data-integrity tooling.

title: FlowLens
summary: A Visual Studio extension that turns ASP.NET Core request paths into interactive source-linked graphs using Roslyn semantic analysis.
description: FlowLens is a Visual Studio extension that analyses ASP.NET Core execution paths and turns them into interactive graphs. It traces an HTTP endpoint through controller actions, DI interfaces, concrete services, repositories and Entity Framework Core operations.
problem: Understanding a complex ASP.NET Core endpoint often requires manually tracing calls across controllers, interfaces, services, repositories and projects. Traditional debugging is not always the fastest way to understand static request structure.
solution: I built an IDE-integrated tool that accepts a controller action, analyses the Roslyn workspace, recursively traces method and dependency relationships, identifies EF Core operations and renders an interactive Overview or Deep Dive graph with direct source navigation.
contributions: Designed and developed the Roslyn analysis engine, endpoint discovery, DI resolution, recursive tracing, EF Core operation classification, graph metadata, Visual Studio VSIX host, WPF/WebView2 tool window, Next.js React interface, ELK graph layout, theme support, progressive expansion and source navigation.
architecture: FlowLens separates static analysis, IDE integration and graph presentation. FlowLens.Core targets netstandard2.0 and uses Microsoft.CodeAnalysis Roslyn. FlowLens.VisualStudio targets .NET Framework 4.7.2 and hosts WPF/WebView2 inside Visual Studio. The UI is a statically exported Next.js application packaged inside the VSIX.
challenges: Call graphs must resolve interfaces and implementations across projects without relying on fragile text searches. Roslyn semantic symbols and recursive traversal provide reliable relationships. Large graphs are managed through Overview and Deep Dive exploration, while ELK layout and source metadata connect visual nodes back to exact code locations.
outcomes: Built an IDE-integrated request-flow visualiser with semantic endpoint, dependency and EF Core analysis, interactive graph exploration, direct source navigation, VSIX packaging and automated tests. The SentinelOps sample demonstrates tracing across controllers, services, repositories and EF Core.

title: Speculintel
summary: A digital intelligence platform in development for unified website, repository, security, performance and technical-quality assessment.
description: Speculintel is a digital intelligence and security platform being developed to give organisations one workspace for website, repository, security, performance and technical-quality insights. The implemented foundation currently includes identity, workspaces, memberships, projects and website targets.
problem: Website, service, dependency and repository health are often assessed with disconnected tools that produce different formats and findings. Before resource-intensive scanning, the platform needs secure account, workspace and digital-asset boundaries.
solution: I am developing a modular .NET 10 backend and Next.js foundation for accounts, workspaces, memberships, projects and website targets. Planned scanning jobs, workers and adapters will eventually turn external website and repository checks into normalised findings and reports.
contributions: Established the solution architecture and implemented identity, account, workspace, membership, project and website-target workflows. Configured PostgreSQL, EF Core migrations, API boundaries, URL policy validation, frontend foundations, engineering standards, documentation and a phased roadmap.
architecture: The current backend uses Domain, Application, Infrastructure, API and Worker projects. Domain owns entities and invariants, Application coordinates use cases, Infrastructure implements Identity and PostgreSQL, API provides HTTP contracts, and Worker is the foundation for future background processing. ASP.NET Core Identity and PostgreSQL provide the implemented foundation.
challenges: The foundation must establish ownership and access boundaries before external URLs or repositories are processed. Future scanning is intentionally designed as bounded asynchronous jobs with explicit states, normalised findings and retries rather than long-running HTTP operations. SSRF protection, least privilege and secret handling remain core design requirements.
outcomes: Established the .NET 10 and PostgreSQL foundation, account and workspace workflows, membership rules, project and website-target models, EF Core migrations, Next.js foundations and a structured roadmap. The repository identifies Phases 0–6 as complete; scanning engines and automation remain planned.

title: Luminar Learning
summary: A multi-role tutoring marketplace for learning pathways, bookings, payments, provider earnings, verification and reporting.
description: Luminar Learning is a full-stack tutoring marketplace connecting students, independent tutors and educational academies. It brings together learning pathways, live tutoring, enrolments, lesson management, provider verification, payments, wallets and reporting.
problem: Tutoring operations often separate registration, tutor discovery, learning content, scheduling, payments and administration. Coordinating lesson completion, provider earnings and student progress across independent tutors and academies requires consistent role and financial boundaries.
solution: I developed a multi-role marketplace for students, independent tutors, academy staff and platform administrators. The platform supports learning pathways, bookings, enrolments, OTP lesson verification, PayFast checkout, refunds, provider wallets, withdrawals and role-scoped reporting.
contributions: Designed and developed the Clean Architecture ASP.NET Core API, Next.js frontend and financial workflows. Implemented Identity and role authorisation, learning pathways, enrolments, live tutoring, OTP verification, PayFast ITN processing, ledgers and wallets, verification, reports and integrations with Cloudinary, R2, SMTP and Python document rendering.
architecture: Luminar follows Clean Architecture. Domain owns core entities and rules, Application coordinates use cases and validation, Infrastructure implements EF Core and external providers, and API provides controllers and middleware. Next.js handles role-specific experiences, while a separate Python FastAPI service renders PDF documents.
architectureFlow: Cloudinary, R2, SMTP and PDF service
challenges: Multiple roles and sensitive financial transitions required strict server-side boundaries and atomic updates. Payment and enrolment changes are committed together, while slower fulfilment and receipt work is handled separately. Provider earnings track held and available balances, and OTP verification provides an additional lesson-completion control.
outcomes: Built a multi-role tutoring marketplace with learning pathways, enrolments, bookings, OTP verification, PayFast payments, provider ledgers and withdrawals, verification workflows, role-scoped exports, health checks, background fulfilment and CI/CD pipelines.
